title: Scope, Authorization & Knowing When to Stop
summary: Learn how training, supervision, authorization, and scope determine whether you should proceed, pause, stop, or escalate.
objectives: Explain why being willing to help does not automatically mean being authorized to act.
Recognize common reasons to pause or stop a task.
Choose an appropriate escalation path when work exceeds your role or training.

vocab.def: Formal permission to perform a task, enter an area, operate equipment, or make a decision.
The boundaries of work, responsibility, training, or authority assigned to a person.
To discontinue an action when continuing may be unsafe, unauthorized, or outside established procedure.
Routing a concern or decision to someone with the appropriate responsibility or authority.

sections.heading: Good intentions do not replace authorization
sections.body: Trying to help can create risk if you perform work you are not trained, supervised, qualified, or authorized to perform.

sections.heading: Know the reasons to pause
sections.body: You may need to pause when instructions are unclear, conditions change, required supervision is absent, protective measures are missing, or the task appears outside your assigned scope.

sections.heading: Stopping can be a professional action
sections.body: A responsible worker does not continue simply because work has already started. Stopping and seeking guidance may prevent a larger problem.

sections.heading: Escalate to the correct authority
sections.body: Escalation should be directed to the person or process designated by the workplace, such as a supervisor, safety lead, instructor, qualified professional, or emergency process.

practice.prompt: You are told to operate equipment you have never been trained to use. What should you do?
practice.answer: Do not operate it until appropriate training, supervision, and authorization are confirmed.

practice.prompt: You begin a task and realize the actual situation does not match the instructions you were given. What should happen?
practice.answer: Pause, identify the mismatch, and clarify or escalate before continuing.

quiz.question: When is stopping work an appropriate response?
options: When continuing may be unsafe, unauthorized, unclear, or outside your scope
Never, if a supervisor originally assigned the task
Only when the task is difficult
quiz.answer: When continuing may be unsafe, unauthorized, unclear, or outside your scope

lab.objective: Classify simulated workplace situations as proceed, pause and clarify, stop, or escalate, and explain the reasoning without performing any hazardous action.
